{{Short description|Concept in chemistry}}
In [[chemical graph theory]], the '''Padmakar–Ivan (PI) index''' is a [[topological index]] of a [[molecule]], used in [[biochemistry]]. The Padmakar–Ivan index is a generalization introduced by [[Padmakar V. Khadikar]] and [[Iván Gutman]]<ref>{{citation|title=A Novel PI Index and Its Applications to QSPR/QSAR Studies
|year=2001|last1=Padmakar|first1=V. Khadikar.|last2=Sneha|first2=Karmarkar|last3=Vijay K.|first3= Agrawal|journal=J. Chem. Inf. Comput. Sci.|volume=41|issue=4|pages=934–949|doi=10.1021/ci0003092|pmid=11500110}}.</ref> of the concept of the [[Wiener index]], introduced by [[Harry Wiener]]. The Padmakar–Ivan index of a graph ''G'' is the sum over all edges  ''uv'' of  ''G'' of number of edges which are not equidistant from ''u''  and ''v''.
Let ''G'' be a graph and ''e''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''uv'' an edge of ''G''. Here <math>n_{eu}(e\mid G)</math> denotes the number of edges lying closer to the vertex ''u'' than the vertex ''v'', and <math>n_{ev}(e\mid G)</math> is the number of edges lying closer to the vertex ''v'' than the vertex ''u''. The Padmakar–Ivan index of a graph ''G'' is defined as

: <math> \operatorname{PI}(G)=\sum_{e\in E(G)}[n_{eu}(e\mid G) + n_{ev}(e\mid G)] </math>

The PI index is very important in the study of [[quantitative structure–activity relationship]] for the classification models used in the [[chemical]], [[biological sciences]], [[engineering]], and [[nanotechnology]].

==Examples==
[[File:Dendrimer Nanostar.png|thumb]]
The PI index of [[Dendrimer]] Nanostar of the following figure can be calculated by<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Khalifeh| first1 = M.H.
 | last2 = Darafsheh| first2 = M.R
 | last3 = Jolany| first3 = H.
 | journal = Journal of Computational and Theoretical Nanoscience
 | pages = 220–223
 | title = The Wiener, Szeged, and PI Indices of a Dendrimer Nanostar
 | volume = 8
 | year = 2011| issue = 2
 | doi = 10.1166/jctn.2011.1681
 | bibcode = 2011JCTN....8..220K
 }}.</ref>

: <math> \operatorname{PI}(G_n) = 441\cdot4^n - 639\cdot2^n + 232, \quad n \geq 0.</math>

The [[double graph]] of a graph <math>G</math>, denoted <math>\mathcal{D}[G]</math>, has a known index in relation to <math>G</math> itself:<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ghasemi |first1=Mehdi |last2=Madanshekaf |first2=Ali |title=On the Topological Indices on Double Graphs |journal=Caspian Journal of Mathematical Sciences |volume=12 |issue=2 |pages=423–439 |date=27 September 2023 |doi=10.22080/CJMS.2023.25624.1660 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

:<math>\operatorname{PI}(\mathcal{D}[G]) = 8\operatorname{PI}(G)</math>
